mainTopic: How jobs were assigned in the תמיד (the פייס, and who collects the blood), and the order in which the limbs were brought to the מזבח.
overview: The amud first finishes the question of whether every עבודה needs its own פייס. רבי יהודה's ברייתא about the מחתה and the קטורת is read both ways, but each reading is pushed off. Then a ברייתא of רבי חייא settles it: the winner of the תמיד draws twelve כהנים along with him. Next, the גמרא asks who does the קבלה of the blood, the שוחט or the זורק. בן קטין's twelve spouts for the כיור prove that the זורק collects, and רב אחא בריה דרבא supports this from a משנה's wording. The amud then turns to the order of carrying the limbs to the מזבח, with four views: walking, skinning, cutting up, and quality. רבא explains that our תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי both go by quality, one by amount of meat and the other by fattiness. Finally, the גמרא explains why the leg goes with the head, and brings a פסוק showing that the head and פדר go first. Its question about a second mention of פדר continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יהודה: No Separate Lottery for the Coal Pan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה's ברייתא to show that one פייס can cover two tasks. The winner of the קטורת simply invited his neighbor to carry the מחתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, there was no lottery for the coal pan. Rather, the כהן who won the incense would say to the one next to him, 'Win along with me the coal pan.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to answer the open question of whether every task needs its own פייס. It brings a ברייתא where the coal-pan job was given out without a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two jobs were involved here. One כהן carried the hot coals in the מחתה, and another put the קטורת on them. רבי יהודה says only the קטורת had a פייס, and the winner chose his partner for the מחתה. That seems to show that one lottery can assign more than one job.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery used to assign jobs to the כהנים
Coal pan: used to carry burning coals to the inner מזבח
Incense burned on the inner מזבח
Win along with me: an invitation to share in the job

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
There was no lottery for the coal pan,
rather, the priest who won the incense
would say to the one who was with him (next to him):
'Win along with me the coal pan.'
phrases.notes: The partner gets the מחתה job without his own lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage with an attempted proof for the earlier question about whether each עבודה needs its own פייס.
steps.raayaObject: That one פייס can assign more than one task, so not every עבודה needs a separate lottery.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה: there was no פייס for the מחתה; the winner of the קטורת invited his neighbor.

steps.title: Rejection: Coal Pan and Incense Are One Service
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The מחתה and the קטורת count as one עבודה, so of course a single פייס covers both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The coal pan and the incense are different, because they are one service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 1. This case is special, so it tells us nothing about other jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing coals and putting incense on them are really two halves of one action, the burning of the קטורת. So one lottery covering both is not like one lottery covering two separate עבודות. The original question is settled later, in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different: a standard way to say a case is special

phrases.english: The coal pan and incense are different,
because they are one service.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מַחְתָּה וּקְטֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by limiting it to a special case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully cancels the proof from רבי יהודה's ברייתא for the first version.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed מחתה and קטורת are two separate עבודות, but they are really one.

steps.title: Second Version: The Same Source Proves the Opposite
steps.stepSummary: איכא דאמרי: the ברייתא is read as a proof the other way. Only מחתה and קטורת share a פייס because they are one עבודה, which implies that all other עבודות need their own פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: specifically the coal pan and incense, which are one service, share a lottery. But other services need a lottery!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the discussion. In this version, the same ברייתא is used to prove that other jobs each need a separate lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version takes the idea from step 2 and turns it into a proof. If רבי יהודה singled out the מחתה because it is part of the same עבודה as the קטורת, then separate עבודות must each need their own פייס. Otherwise, why mention this specific pair?
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a new objection to step 2. It is a separate version of the whole discussion, in which the same ברייתא is used to prove the opposite conclusion.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Specifically the coal pan and incense,
which are one service, (share a lottery);
but other services require a lottery!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version: it uses the 'one עבודה' idea of step 2 as a proof for the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: That every separate עבודה needs its own פייס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the wording of רבי יהודה's ברייתא, which specifically mentions the מחתה with the קטורת.

steps.title: Rejection: The Coal Pan Needed to Be Taught
steps.stepSummary: The second proof is rejected. רבי יהודה mentioned the מחתה only because we might have thought that, being rare and bringing wealth, it deserved its own פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to teach the coal pan. You might have thought that since it is rare and brings wealth, we should set up a separate lottery for it. So he teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof of step 3. There is a special reason why רבי יהודה mentioned the מחתה, so we cannot draw any conclusion about other עבודות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטורת happens only twice a day, and it brings wealth to the one who does it, so many כהנים would want the job. That might have led us to think the מחתה, as part of it, gets its own פייס. רבי יהודה teaches that it does not, so his statement says nothing about other עבודות. The next step settles the question with a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this case)
You might have thought: introduces a mistaken first assumption

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רבי יהודה's ברייתא ends up proving nothing about other עבודות. The מחתה and קטורת share one פייס, either because they are one עבודה or because רבי יהודה needed to teach that even this rare and enriching task gets no separate lottery.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. When a specific case is mentioned, we cannot always infer that other cases are different (דוקא), because the case may have been mentioned to rule out a special reason we might have had.

phrases.english: The coal pan was necessary for him (to mention),
for it would have entered your mind to say:
since it is not common, and it brings wealth,
phrases.notes: This is about the קטורת, done only twice a day, and it brings wealth to whoever offers it.

phrases.english: let us institute a lottery for it by itself.
So he teaches us (that we do not).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְתָּה אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3 by explaining why רבי יהודה needed to mention the מחתה specifically.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully cancels the proof of the second version; the ברייתא proves nothing either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The דוקא inference fails because mentioning the מחתה had its own purpose: to reject the idea that a rare, enriching task gets a separate פייס.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's ברייתא cannot settle whether every עבודה needs its own פייס.

steps.title: רבי חייא's teaching settles it: one lottery pulls in twelve priests
steps.stepSummary: A clear ברייתא of רבי חייא proves there is no separate פייס for every עבודה. The winner of the תמיד brings twelve fellow כהנים with him, and the גמרא concludes 'שמע מינה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבי חייא taught: we do not hold a lottery for each separate service. Instead, the כהן who won the תמיד has twelve of his fellow כהנים drawn in along with him. Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: After two proofs were pushed off, the גמרא brings an explicit ברייתא that answers the question directly, and it closes with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1-4 tried to learn the rule from hints in רבי יהודה's ברייתא, and every hint was rejected. רבי חייא says the rule outright: a single פייס for the תמיד covers the other jobs, which go to the twelve כהנים standing next to the winner. Because the source is explicit, nobody can push it off, so the question is closed.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold a lottery (פַּיִיס) to choose which כהן does a job
The daily communal offering, brought morning and afternoon
Are drawn along with him, so they get jobs without their own lottery
"Learn from this": the proof stands and the question is settled

steps.whatToRemember: One פייס for the תמיד is enough. The winner and the twelve כהנים beside him share the remaining jobs, so there is no separate lottery for each עבודה.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean there is only one פייס in the whole morning. The משנה still lists several separate lotteries. Within the תמיד's group of jobs, though, one win pulls twelve others along.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Chiyya taught:
phrases.notes: A ברייתא is brought as a direct proof.

phrases.english: We do not hold a lottery for each and every service,
rather, the priest who won the daily offering,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים נִמְשָׁכִין עִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: twelve of his fellow priests are drawn in with him.
phrases.notes: These are the כהנים standing next to him in the counting circle.

phrases.english: Learn from this (that it is so).
phrases.notes: Signals that the matter is settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier proofs from רבי יהודה's ברייתא were all rejected. This explicit ברייתא finally decides the question.
steps.raayaObject: That one פייס covers several עבודות of the תמיד, rather than a separate פייס for each.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא: the winner of the תמיד draws twelve fellow כהנים with him.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no separate פייס for each עבודה. The winner of the תמיד and the twelve כהנים next to him take the remaining jobs.

steps.title: Who collects the blood? First option: the slaughterer
steps.stepSummary: Citing the second פייס of the משנה, the גמרא asks who does the קבלה. The first option is the שוחט, because the זורק might rush and not collect all the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The second lottery, etc.' They asked: who collects the blood? Maybe the one who slaughters collects. If you say the one who sprinkles collects, then out of his love for sprinkling he might not collect all the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes the משנה's second פייס, asks who does the קבלה (which the משנה does not mention), and gives the first possible answer with its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the שוחט and the זורק but skips the קבלה, the job in between, so one of those two must do it. Side one says the שוחט. The זורק is eager to reach the more beloved job of זריקה on the מזבח, and in his rush he might stop collecting before all the blood is in the כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them": a real open question (בעיא)
Collects the blood in a vessel (קַבָּלָה)
The one who slaughters the animal
The one who sprinkles the blood on the מִזְבֵּחַ
His fondness or eagerness for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never mentions קבלה at all. That gap is exactly why the גמרא has to ask who does it.

phrases.english: "The second lottery," etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה to start a new discussion.

phrases.english: They asked: who collects (the blood)?
The slaughterer collects,
phrases.notes: First side of the question.

phrases.english: for if you say the sprinkler collects —
because of his eagerness (for sprinkling),
he will not collect all of the blood.
phrases.notes: He might rush on to the זריקה too soon.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּיִיס הַשֵּׁנִי וְכוּ׳. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי מְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier question is closed. This step starts a new question on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which כהן does the קבלה of the תמיד's blood, the שוחט or the זורק?

steps.title: Second option: the sprinkler collects, since a non-priest may slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the question: maybe the זורק collects. The שוחט cannot be relied on for this, because sometimes a זר does the שחיטה, and a זר may not do קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the one who sprinkles collects, because if you say the slaughterer collects, sometimes a non-priest slaughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the opposite side of the question, with its own reason. Steps 8-9 bring a proof that settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר may do שחיטה, because it is not a כהן's job. קבלה must be done by a כהן. So a rule that 'the שוחט collects' would sometimes fail, and the job belongs with the זורק, who is always a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: "Or perhaps": introduces the other side of a question

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key halachic point: שחיטה is valid when done by a זר, but קבלה and onward need a כהן.

phrases.english: Or perhaps the sprinkler collects,
for if you say the slaughterer collects —
sometimes a non-priest slaughters.
phrases.notes: A זר cannot do קבלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא: זוֹרֵק מְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the question opened in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the קבלה should be tied to the זורק, because a שוחט may be a זר.

steps.title: A proof begins: Ben Katin's twelve spouts for the laver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: בן קטין made twelve spouts for the כיור so the twelve כהנים busy with the תמיד could wash at once. The exact inference comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בן קטין made twelve spouts for the laver, so that his twelve fellow priests busy with the תמיד could sanctify their hands and feet at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof to answer the question. It brings the source here, and the argument from it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד uses thirteen כהנים in all, yet only twelve spouts were made. That suggests one participant did not need קידוש ידים ורגלים: the שוחט, since שחיטה is not a כהן's עבודה. The גמרא will use this count to judge whether the שוחט also does the קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול who made improvements to the מקדש
The large laver (washbasin) in the עזרה
Sanctify (wash) their hands and feet before doing the עבודה

steps.confusionAlert: Count carefully: thirteen people work on the תמיד, but only twelve spouts were made. The 'missing' one is the key to the proof.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Ben Katin made
twelve spouts for the laver,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: so that his twelve fellow priests
who are busy with the daily offering
could sanctify their hands and feet at one time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from steps 6-7 using a source about the כיור.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the שוחט or the זורק does the קבלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that בן קטין made twelve spouts so the twelve כהנים of the תמיד could wash together.

steps.title: Twelve spouts prove that the sprinkler collects the blood
steps.stepSummary: If the שוחט did the קבלה, a זר's שחיטה would force an extra כהן to do the קבלה, making thirteen. The spouts are only twelve, so the זורק must be the one who collects.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think the slaughterer is the one who collects the blood, then there would sometimes be thirteen! Rather, is it not clear from here that the sprinkler collects? Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now draws the exact inference from בן קטין's twelve spouts and settles the question from Steps 6–7: the זורק does the קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a זר slaughters the תמיד, and a זר may not do קבלה. If the job of collecting belonged to the שוחט, a thirteenth כהן would have to be added to collect, and he too would need to wash. Since בן קטין made exactly twelve spouts for exactly twelve כהנים, the collector must already be one of the twelve, namely the זורק.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it should enter your mind (introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to reject)
Rather, is it not clear from here?
The כהן who sprinkles the blood on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer to the second פייס: the זורק is the one who does the קבלה, not the שוחט.

phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind
that the slaughterer collects the blood,
phrases.notes: This is the first side of the question from Step 6.

phrases.english: there would be thirteen!
phrases.notes: When a זר slaughters, an extra כהן would be needed to collect the blood.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not clear from this:
the sprinkler collects the blood.
Learn it from this.
phrases.notes: The proof is accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ שׁוֹחֵט מְקַבֵּל, תְּלֵיסַר הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 8 by drawing the inference from the number twelve.
steps.raayaObject: That the זורק, not the שוחט, does the קבלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about בן קטין's twelve spouts for the twelve כהנים of the תמיד
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: זורק מקבל: the one who sprinkles is the one who collects.

steps.title: Support from the wording of a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא tells רב אשי that a משנה already says this: the collector is the one who then goes to sprinkle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: We also learned this in a משנה: 'The slaughterer slaughtered, the collector collected, and he comes to sprinkle.' Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: A second support is brought for the same conclusion, this time from the exact wording of a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'the collector collected, and he comes to sprinkle.' The word 'he' points back to the collector. So the same כהן who collects is the one who sprinkles, which matches the conclusion of Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה): a formula for bringing extra support

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
We too have learned it:
The slaughterer slaughtered,
and the collector collected,
and he comes to sprinkle.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the collector, so the collector is the sprinkler.

phrases.english: Learn it from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent source supporting Step 9's conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: That the collector is also the sprinkler
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה describing the order of the services: 'and he comes to sprinkle'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wording of the משנה confirms that the מקבל is the זורק.

steps.title: Order of the limbs according to the way the animal walks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites בן עזאי's statement from the משנה and brings a ברייתא explaining 'the way it walks': front parts first, back parts last.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: בן עזאי said before רבי עקיבא, etc. The רבנן taught: How does 'the way it walks' work? The head and the right hind leg; the breast and the neck; the two forelegs; the two flanks; the tail and the left hind leg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה, the order of carrying the limbs to the מזבח. A ברייתא spells out בן עזאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal walks, its front goes first. So the limbs are brought from front to back. The head and right hind leg always go first, and then the order moves forward-to-back: breast and neck, forelegs, flanks, and finally the tail with the left hind leg.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two 'legs' (רגל) in every list. The first is the right hind leg, which is brought with the head. The second is the left hind leg, which is brought with the tail. Do not read them as the same leg.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Ben Azzai said before Rabbi Akiva, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה being explained.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How does 'the way it walks' work?
The head and the (right hind) leg,
the breast and the neck,
and the two forelegs,
and the two flanks,
the tail and the (left hind) leg.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה, the order of carrying the limbs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the way it walks: head and right leg, breast and neck, forelegs, flanks, tail and left leg.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the order of skinning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the limbs were brought in the order the animal is skinned, which ends with the breast and neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: It was offered in the order of its skinning. How? The head and the right leg; the tail and the left leg; the two flanks; the two forelegs; the breast and the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second view. רבי יוסי orders the limbs by how the animal's hide is removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal hangs by its hind legs and is skinned from the back end downward. So the back parts come early (tail and left leg) and the breast and neck come last. This is close to the reverse of בן עזאי's front-to-back order.

keyTerms.meaning: It was offered (brought up to the מזבח)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It was offered in the order of its skinning.
How does 'the order of skinning' work?
The head and the (right) leg,
the tail and the (left) leg,
and the two flanks,
and the two forelegs,
the breast and the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: דֶּרֶךְ הֶפְשֵׁטוֹ הָיָה קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing opinion to בן עזאי's order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to skinning: head and right leg, tail and left leg, flanks, forelegs, breast and neck.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the order of cutting up
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the limbs were brought in the order the animal is cut into pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: It was offered in the order of its cutting up. How? The head and the right leg; the two forelegs; the breast and the neck; the two flanks; the tail and the left leg.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view in the ברייתא. רבי עקיבא follows the order in which the butchering is done after skinning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is different from בן עזאי only in one place: the forelegs come before the breast and neck. That is because the forelegs are cut off first in the butchering process.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of its cutting into limbs

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
It was offered in the order of its cutting up.
How does 'the order of cutting up' work?
The head and the (right) leg,
and the two forelegs,
the breast and the neck,
and the two flanks,
and the tail and the (left) leg.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: דֶּרֶךְ נִיתּוּחוֹ הָיָה קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion on the same question of order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to cutting up: head and right leg, forelegs, breast and neck, flanks, tail and left leg.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the order of quality
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the best pieces were brought first and the forelegs last.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: It was offered in the order of its quality. How? The head and the right leg; the breast and the neck; the two flanks; the tail and the left leg; the two forelegs.
steps.whatsHappening: The fourth and last view in the ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי ranks the limbs by how choice the meat is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The finer, choicer parts go up first. The forelegs, which are the least choice, go last. All four views agree that the head and right leg are brought first. They argue only about the order of the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of its quality (best pieces first)

steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on the order of the limbs: by walking (בן עזאי), skinning (רבי יוסי), cutting up (רבי עקיבא), and quality (רבי יוסי הגלילי). All four start with the head and the right hind leg.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
It was offered in the order of its quality.
How does 'the order of quality' work?
The head and the (right) leg,
the breast and the neck,
and the two flanks,
and the tail and the (left) leg,
and the two forelegs.
phrases.notes: The forelegs come last because they are the least choice.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: דֶּרֶךְ עִילּוּיוֹ הָיָה קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to quality: head and right leg, breast and neck, flanks, tail and left leg, forelegs.

steps.title: A verse seems to say the thigh and shoulder are the best pieces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי with a פסוק in יחזקאל that calls the thigh and shoulder the 'good pieces'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'Every good piece, the thigh and the shoulder'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said the best pieces go up first. A פסוק calls the thigh and shoulder the best pieces, so why doesn't he put them first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule is 'best pieces first.' The פסוק seems to tell us which pieces are best: the thigh and the shoulder. If so, his order should start with them, but it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
A piece or cut of meat

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'Every good piece,'
phrases.notes: From יחזקאל כד:ד.

phrases.english: 'the thigh and the shoulder'?
phrases.notes: The פסוק seems to name these as the best pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי stated in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's order of 'best pieces first'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק defines the thigh and shoulder as the best pieces, yet his order does not put them first.

steps.title: That verse is talking about a lean animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in יחזקאל speaks about a skinny animal, unlike the high-quality תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is about a lean animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the פסוק describes a lean, skinny animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a skinny animal the thigh and shoulder really are the best parts. But the תמיד was a fat, top-quality animal, and in such an animal other parts are better. So the פסוק does not contradict רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: That verse is about a lean animal.
phrases.notes: In a fat animal like the תמיד, other parts are better.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא בִּכְחוּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to a different case (a lean animal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק says the thigh and shoulder are always the best pieces.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only applies to a lean animal; in the fat תמיד, other pieces are better.

steps.title: רבא explains the real dispute: amount of meat versus fattiness
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both our תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי order the limbs by quality, but they measure quality differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both our תנא and רבי יוסי follow the quality of the meat. One Sage goes by the amount of meat, and the other goes by the fattiness of the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that our תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי actually share the same idea: the better pieces go first. They only disagree about what makes a piece 'better'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תנא measures quality by how much meat is on the limb. רבי יוסי הגלילי measures quality by how fatty the meat is. That one difference explains why their orders come out different.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the author of our משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי יוסי here is רבי יוסי הגלילי from step 14, not the plain רבי יוסי of step 12.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין תַּנָּא דִּידַן וּבֵין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: Both our tanna and Rabbi Yosei —
phrases.notes: Meaning רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: we follow the quality of the meat.
One Sage goes by the amount of the meat,
phrases.notes: Our תנא.

phrases.english: and the other Sage goes by the fattiness of the meat.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בֵּין תַּנָּא דִּידַן וּבֵין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוסי הגלילי, the גמרא explains how his view relates to our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions order the limbs by quality; our תנא judges by amount of meat, רבי יוסי הגלילי by fattiness.

steps.title: Why does the leg go up together with the head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, according to everyone, the רגל is brought together with the ראש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that the leg goes up together with the head?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: why is the right leg paired with the head when the limbs are brought up?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head and the leg are not next to each other on the animal, so it is unclear why they travel together. The גמרא wants the reason behind this pairing.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא סָלְקָא רֶגֶל בַּהֲדֵי רֵישָׁא?
phrases.english: What is the reason that the leg goes up together with the head?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא סָלְקָא רֶגֶל בַּהֲדֵי רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute to a detail everyone agrees on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רגל is paired with the ראש.

steps.title: The head is mostly bone, so the leg is added to it
steps.stepSummary: The head has a lot of bone and little meat, so the leg goes with it to balance the load.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the head has many bones in it, the leg is offered with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the head is mostly bone, so the leg is brought with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the head has little meat, it is not a full portion by itself. Adding the leg makes it a proper portion for one כהן to carry.

phrases.english: Because the head has many bones in it,
the leg is offered with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרֵישָׁא נְפִישִׁי בֵּיהּ עֲצָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The head is mostly bone, so the leg is paired with it.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the head goes first: what is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that all opinions put the ראש first and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: At any rate, everyone agrees the head is offered first. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that, despite all the arguments about the order, every opinion starts with the head. It now asks for the source of that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opinions disagree about the rest of the order, but the head being first is shared. A shared rule like this needs a source, so the גמרא asks for one.

phrases.english: At any rate, according to everyone,
the head is offered first,
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת רֹאשׁ קָרֵב בְּרֵישָׁא, מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the point all the opinions in steps 11-14 share.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the ראש is offered before the other limbs.

steps.title: A ברייתא derives it from the verse 'its head and its fat'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ויקרא א:יב that the ראש and פדר come before all the other limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: From where do we know that the head and the fat come before all the limbs? The verse says: 'its head and its fat, and he shall arrange.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The פסוק names the head and the fat first, which shows they go up before everything else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא א:יב the Torah mentions 'its head and its fat' right before 'and he shall arrange.' The ברייתא reads this order as an instruction: the head and the fat are placed first. This gives the source that every opinion relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat (a layer of fat covering the place of slaughter)

steps.whatToRemember: All opinions agree the ראש goes first, together with the פדר, learned from 'אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ וְאֶת פִּדְרוֹ וְעָרַךְ'.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
From where do we know that the head and the fat
come before all the limbs?
The verse says:
'its head and its fat, and he shall arrange.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:יב.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִין לְרֹאשׁ וּפֶדֶר שֶׁקּוֹדְמִין לְכׇל הָאֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ וְאֶת פִּדְרוֹ וְעָרַךְ' shows the head and fat come first.

steps.title: What does the other mention of 'fat' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask about a second mention of פדר in an earlier פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other mention of 'fat' — what does it teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that 'fat' is mentioned in another פסוק too (ויקרא א:ח). It begins to ask what that extra mention teaches; the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one פסוק already teaches that the head and fat go first, a second mention of פדר seems extra. The גמרא assumes the Torah has no extra words, so the second mention must teach something new. This line sets up the next move.

phrases.english: And the other, second mention of 'fat'?
phrases.notes: The other mention is in ויקרא א:ח. The question continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: ״פָּדֶר״ אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the ברייתא of step 21 by asking about the extra mention of פדר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second mention of פדר in ויקרא א:ח comes to teach.
